newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki slips on Wall Street losses.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki slips on Wall Street losses.

text.p: Shares closed a moderately active session lower on Wednesday, ending a four-day rally. Sentiment was dampened by overnight losses on Wall Street, brokers said.
The HEX index fell 0.67 percent to 2,142.24. Volume was a fair 329 million markka.
The central bank's 15 basis point cut in its key tender rate to 3.10 percent did not invigorate the bourse as the focus was on the jittery U.S. stock and bond markets, brokers said.
Retailer and wholesaler Kesko lost 2.40 markka to close at 71.60 after saying the EU Commission had made a preliminary finding that its acquisition of rival Tuko may be against merger laws.
Telecom group Nokia fell 4.00 markka to 193.50 despite news that Goldman Sachs initiated it with an outperform rating. The share accounted for 25 percent of bourse turnover.

Data services group TT Tieto advanced 20.00 markka to a 270.00 life high on continued brisk foreign demand. Some brokers said the share was still benefitting from a week-old buy recommendation from Merrill Lynch.

Forestries continued to ease amid speculation of a possible linkage of the markka to the European exchange rate mechanism. UPM-Kymmene closed flat at 99.50, but Metsa-Serla was off one markka at 32.50.
